key_insight: Neural networks can be transformed into equivalent logic-flow programs that replace many MAC-heavy operations with control-flow and Boolean primitives, making inference far more efficient on CPU-only edge devices.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between MAC-dominated neural inference and the control-flow–optimized architecture of low-power edge CPUs, enabling accurate NN deployment without GPUs or high MAC throughput.
method: Extract and quantize network behavior into discrete (often Boolean/binarized) representations and rule-like decision paths.
Transform layers into logic-flow graphs (if/else, lookup tables, Boolean networks) and apply synthesis/optimization (pruning, minimization).
Map optimized logic flows to CPU-friendly implementations and evaluate performance, energy, and accuracy on edge benchmarks.
impact: Enables low-latency, low-power inference on ubiquitous CPU-only edge devices, expanding practical deployment of ML in IoT and embedded systems while reducing reliance on specialized accelerators.
visual_elements: Conversion pipeline diagram: trained NN → quantization/rule extraction → logic-flow graph → CPU implementation
Bar chart comparing MAC count, latency, and energy: original NN vs logic-flow implementation
Schematic showing CPU-friendly primitives (if/else, LUTs, bitwise ops) replacing dense MAC blocks
Before/after accuracy vs. power scatter plot to show trade-offs
paper_title: Late Breaking Results: Conversion of Neural Networks into Logic Flows for Edge Computing
paper_authors: Daniel Stein, Shaoyi Huang, Rolf Drechsler, Bing Li, Grace Li Zhang
